reports.title: Instituto Nacional de Estadística e Informática (INEI) — institutional statistical identity
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística e Informática
reports.description: National statistical office of Peru. Produces the core official statistics (prices, household surveys, poverty, national accounts inputs, census, etc.) and coordinates the national statistical system.
reports._notes: Institutional parent node for Peruvian official statistics. Continuously cited as the producer of the principal economic and social series.
_referenced_by: All major INEI programme methodologies and technical reports
Banco Central de Reserva statistical publications that cite INEI sources

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Hogares (ENAHO) / National Household Survey
reports.description: Continuous household survey that is the official source for living conditions, monetary poverty, multidimensional poverty, income and expenditure, education and health access. National coverage with departmental disaggregation.
reports._notes: Central social survey of Peru. Continuous since 2003 (earlier quarterly from 1995). Primary microdata source for poverty measurement and for a wide range of living-conditions indicators. Quarterly living-conditions reports and annual poverty results are the main public products.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria / Monetary poverty
reports.description: Official income/expenditure-based poverty and extreme-poverty incidence. Calculated by comparing household per-capita expenditure (from ENAHO) with nationally defined poverty lines. Annual publication with urban/rural and departmental breakdowns.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator. 2025: monetary poverty 25.7% (down 1.9 pp from 27.6% in 2024); extreme poverty 4.7%. Urban–rural gap remains large (urban ~23.4%, rural ~35.5%). Series supervised by the Comisión Consultiva.

reports.title: Líneas de pobreza total y extrema
reports.description: Monetary values of the total and extreme poverty lines (per capita and for reference households), updated with price information and differentiated by geographic domain.
reports._notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. 2025 total poverty line ~S/ 462 per person; extreme (basic food basket) ~S/ 260 per person.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services. National and major-city coverage.
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic. Direct input into monetary-policy analysis by the Banco Central de Reserva and into the updating of poverty lines.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Peru
reports.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income. Quarterly and annual releases.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. INEI is the primary compiler of the real-sector accounts.

reports.title: Encuesta Permanente de Empleo Nacional (EPEN) / Permanent National Employment Survey
reports.description: Continuous employment survey providing labour-force indicators (employment, unemployment, underemployment, informality) at national and major-domain levels.
reports._notes: Primary high-frequency labour survey. Complements the longer-running ENAHO on labour-market dimensions and feeds the quarterly living-conditions reports.

reports.title: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú — statistical publications (monetary, external, inflation)
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Central-bank statistical output covering monetary aggregates, balance of payments, international reserves, exchange rates, and inflation analysis. Complements INEI’s real-sector and price statistics.
reports._notes: In the Peruvian division of labour INEI leads national accounts, prices, household surveys and poverty; the BCR leads monetary, external and financial statistics and conducts inflation-targeting policy.

reports.title: Censos Nacionales de Población y Vivienda / National Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline, sampling frames for household surveys, and small-area population estimates.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product. Continuously cited by ENAHO/EPEN design, poverty analysis and departmental statistical work.

reports.title: Condiciones de Vida en el Perú (quarterly technical report)
reports.description: Quarterly technical report synthesising ENAHO and EPEN results on living conditions, employment and related welfare indicators.
reports._notes: Regular public synthesis product. Bridges the continuous survey data to a widely used quarterly narrative on welfare and the labour market.

reports.title: Producción Nacional / Monthly GDP (PBI)
reports.description: Monthly estimate of national production (PBI) by economic activity. Principal high-frequency real-activity indicator.
reports._notes: Core short-term activity product. 2025 full-year growth ~3.4%; Q1 2026 ~3.5%. Construction, commerce and manufacturing have been recent drivers.

reports.title: PBI Manufactura / Manufacturing production
reports.description: Volume and value indicators of manufacturing production, split into primary and non-primary manufacturing. Monthly and annual series.
reports._notes: Manufacturing contributes ~12% of GDP. 2025 growth ~2.7% (primary +4.9%, non-primary +1.9%). Export-oriented manufacturing has been a notable contributor.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product. Recent years have shown current-account surpluses driven by strong traditional exports (mining, fishing, gas). Net international investment position and reserve adequacy are regularly reported.

reports.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
reports.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods, classified as traditional (mining, fishing, agriculture, oil/gas) and non-traditional.
reports._notes: Trade data feed both the BOP and the national accounts. Mining remains the dominant traditional export; manufacturing exports have shown strong recent growth.

reports.title: Reporte de Inflación (BCR)
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Periodic Inflation Report of the central bank. Explains recent inflation, the outlook, and the implications for the reference interest rate under the explicit inflation-targeting regime.
reports._notes: Flagship policy communication product. Complements the monthly monetary-programme statements. Central reference for the 1–3% inflation target band.

reports.title: Tasa de interés de referencia / Policy interest rate
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Main monetary-policy instrument of the BCR Board. The rate at which the central bank signals the monetary stance and steers interbank rates.
reports._notes: Operational policy rate. Held at 4.25% for an extended period in 2025–2026 after the earlier easing cycle. Path is the primary signal of the monetary stance.

reports.title: Reservas Internacionales Netas (RIN)
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Stock of net international reserves managed by the central bank. Published at high frequency and analysed in the BOP and annual reports.
reports._notes: Key external-buffer indicator. End-2025 RIN ~USD 90 bn (~26% of GDP), covering multiple months of imports and a high multiple of short-term external debt.

reports.title: Marco de metas de inflación (1–3%) — BCR
reports.publisher: Banco Central de Reserva del Perú
reports.description: Operational monetary-policy framework: explicit inflation targeting with a 1–3% annual CPI band (centre 2%). In place since 2002.
reports._notes: Core policy-framework node. Continuously cited as the reference against which inflation outcomes and policy actions are evaluated.
_referenced_by: Every Inflation Report and monetary-programme statement
IPC and inflation analysis that refers to the target band
Market and academic commentary on Peruvian monetary policy

reports.title: Producción y exportaciones mineras / Mining production & exports
reports.publisher: INEI / Ministerio de Energía y Minas / BCR
reports.description: Statistics of metallic and non-metallic mining production and exports (copper, gold, zinc, silver, etc.). Structural component of traditional exports and of GDP.
reports._notes: Mining is the backbone of traditional exports and a major GDP contributor. Copper and gold dominate the export basket; production and export volumes are high-frequency inputs into the BOP and national accounts.

reports.title: Producción y exportaciones pesqueras / Fishing & fishmeal
reports.description: Statistics of fishing catch, fishmeal and fish-oil production and exports. Important traditional export and source of short-term volatility in manufacturing and GDP.
reports._notes: High-volatility traditional sector. Anchovy/fishmeal cycles drive large swings in primary manufacturing and in the goods trade balance. Regularly highlighted in monthly production and BOP analysis.

reports.title: Lima Metropolitana — capital statistical identity
reports.description: Capital metropolitan area and largest urban economy. Primary high-frequency domain for ENAHO, EPEN and many price/activity series. Intermediate monetary-poverty incidence relative to the national average.
reports._notes: Dominant metro node. 2025 monetary poverty in Lima Metropolitana ~27.3% (close to the national 25.7%). Continuously published as a distinct geographic domain in poverty and living-conditions reports.

reports.title: Departamento de Cajamarca — highest-poverty contrast
reports.description: Andean department with the highest monetary-poverty incidence in the 2025 results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under persistent high poverty despite mining presence.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast department. 2025 monetary poverty 41.0% (highest); also among the highest in extreme poverty. Has remained in the top poverty group for many consecutive years.

reports.title: Departamento de Loreto — high-poverty Selva contrast
reports.description: Amazonian department with the second-highest monetary-poverty incidence. Completes the periphery contrast alongside Cajamarca and Puno.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 40.1%. Illustrates the Selva high-poverty cluster under a common national measurement framework.

reports.title: Departamento de Puno — high-poverty Sierra contrast
reports.description: Southern Andean department ranking among the highest in monetary and extreme poverty.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 37.5%. Part of the persistent high-poverty Sierra group.

reports.title: Departamento de Ica — low-poverty contrast
reports.description: Coastal department with the lowest monetary-poverty incidence in the 2025 results.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty 4.5% — lowest of the departments. Completes the low-poverty pole opposite Cajamarca/Loreto/Puno.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria por departamento (INEI)
reports.description: Official departmental tabulations of monetary poverty and extreme poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
reports._notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking (selected): Cajamarca 41.0%, Loreto 40.1%, Puno 37.5%, … Ica 4.5%, Madre de Dios 7.3%, Moquegua 7.8%. National average 25.7%.

reports.title: Alianza del Pacífico (Protocolo Comercial)
reports.publisher: Estados miembros de la Alianza del Pacífico (Chile, Colombia, México, Perú)
reports.description: Regional integration initiative and commercial protocol among the four Pacific-facing Latin American economies. Preferential trade, investment and regulatory cooperation framework.
reports._notes: Latin American Pacific counterpart to MERCOSUR. Continuously cited in official trade reporting.
_referenced_by: Peruvian trade-agreement monitoring and MinCETUR reports
Export and import statistics with AP partners

reports.title: Presupuesto del Sector Público / National Budget (MEF)
reports.description: Annual public-sector budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the central government and transfers.
reports._notes: Operational fiscal framework. 2026 budget ~S/ 257.6 bn. Education, health, transport and security absorb a large share of the functional allocation.

reports.title: Estadísticas de educación / Education statistics & budget
reports.description: Enrolment, attainment and learning-outcome indicators together with the education functional budget. Complements ENAHO education modules.
reports._notes: Education is a major budget priority. ENAHO provides household-side attainment and access data; administrative systems and learning assessments supply the supply-side picture.

reports.title: Estadísticas de salud / Health coverage & expenditure
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Salud / SIS / INEI / MEF
reports.description: Health-insurance coverage (SIS and other schemes), health-service access and the health functional budget. Complements ENAHO health modules.
reports._notes: Health is a major and growing budget function. SIS (Seguro Integral de Salud) is the principal public insurer for the uninsured population; ENAHO tracks affiliation and access.

reports.title: Café — producción y exportaciones
reports.publisher: MIDAGRI / Junta Nacional del Café / SUNAT / INEI
reports.description: Statistics of coffee production and exports. Leading traditional agricultural export, produced mainly by smallholders in Andean and Amazonian foothill regions. Peru is a major organic-coffee exporter.
reports._notes: Signature soft-commodity export. 2025 exports reached record levels (reports in the USD 1.7–1.8 bn range). Produced in 16 regions; main producers include San Martín, Cajamarca, Junín, Cusco and Amazonas. Continuously cited in agro-export and rural-economy analysis.

reports.title: Agroexportaciones / Non-traditional agricultural exports
reports.description: Broader statistics of agricultural and agro-industrial exports (fresh produce, processed foods, coffee, cocoa, etc.). Complements the mining-dominated traditional-export basket.
reports._notes: Non-traditional agro-exports have been a diversification success story. Coffee is the largest single traditional agricultural line; blueberries, grapes, avocados and asparagus are major non-traditional lines.

reports.title: Tratado de Libre Comercio Perú–Estados Unidos
reports.description: Bilateral free-trade agreement in force since February 2009. Core preferential-access instrument for the US market and a recurring reference in trade and investment analysis.
reports._notes: Major bilateral FTA. Continuously cited in official trade-performance reporting. Nearly all Peruvian tariff lines enter the US duty-free under the agreement.
_referenced_by: Export statistics by partner (US is a top destination for coffee and other agro-exports)
Policy debates on market access and diversification

reports.title: Tratado de Libre Comercio Perú–China
reports.publisher: Gobierno del Perú / República Popular China
reports.description: Bilateral free-trade agreement in force since March 2010. Underpins the large and growing bilateral trade relationship, especially mining and agricultural exports to China.
reports._notes: Structurally important bilateral instrument. China is a top destination for Peruvian copper and other minerals; the FTA is routinely cited in explanations of the trade relationship.
_referenced_by: Official monitoring of the China FTA

reports.title: Sierra — natural-region statistical domain
reports.description: Andean highlands natural region used as a standard geographic domain in ENAHO poverty and living-conditions analysis. Highest rural poverty incidence.
reports._notes: Key natural-region domain. Sierra rural recorded the highest monetary poverty in 2025 (~38.8%). Hosts much of the coffee and highland agricultural production as well as important mining districts.

reports.title: Selva — natural-region statistical domain
reports.description: Amazonian natural region used as a standard geographic domain in ENAHO analysis. Elevated rural poverty and important coffee/cocoa producing zones.
reports._notes: Selva rural poverty remains elevated (~30.7% in 2025). Contains major coffee-producing departments such as San Martín and parts of Amazonas.

reports.title: Costa — natural-region statistical domain
reports.description: Coastal natural region used as a standard geographic domain. Lowest poverty incidence among the three natural regions; hosts the capital and the bulk of non-traditional agro-exports.
reports._notes: Costa urbana has the lowest poverty rates. Completes the three natural-region domains (Costa–Sierra–Selva) that structure much of Peruvian social and agricultural analysis.

reports.title: Departamento de San Martín — coffee-producing Andean–Amazon transition
reports.description: Major coffee-producing department in the Andean–Amazon transition zone. Important for both agricultural-export and rural-poverty analysis.
reports._notes: One of the leading coffee regions. Links the commodity (coffee) to the departmental and natural-region poverty/production geography.

reports.title: Canon minero y regalías mineras
reports.publisher: MEF / Ministerio de Energía y Minas
reports.description: Mining canon and royalty transfers from central government to producing regions and local governments. Major sub-national fiscal mechanism linking mining production to territorial budgets.
reports._notes: Critical sub-national fiscal node. Directly links the mining production and export statistics to departmental and municipal budgets, especially in the Sierra and mining corridors.

reports.title: Departamento de Moquegua — low-poverty mining contrast
reports.description: Southern mining department with very low monetary-poverty incidence. Completes the mining-department contrast alongside Ica.
reports._notes: 2025 monetary poverty ~7.8%. Hosts major copper operations; illustrates that mining presence can coincide with low measured poverty under the national framework.

dependencies.basis: Monetary poverty is calculated from ENAHO household expenditure and income data.

Poverty lines are updated with price information derived from the IPC.

Pacific Alliance preferential trade is a recurring analytical dimension of merchandise-trade reporting.

The US FTA underpins preferential bilateral trade flows, including coffee and other agro-exports.
The China FTA underpins the large bilateral trade relationship, especially minerals.
Canon and royalties are generated by mining production.
San Martín is one of the principal coffee-producing departments.

_consolidation.json_syntax_repair_note: These batch files were not valid JSON as delivered: "releases_per_year" carried an unquoted text value (missing opening quote), e.g. `"releases_per_year": continuous",`. Repaired mechanically by re-quoting the value verbatim. No number was invented.
_consolidation.cadence_note: A non-numeric cadence text was moved off releases_per_year into _cadence_original verbatim and the numeric field omitted, per the v2 spec (omitted, never null). Needs a human/judgement pass to become a real number.

_normalisation.note: Second pass, 2026-08-18: mechanical alignment to src/lib/types.ts. Nothing researched, nothing invented. Every original value that was replaced is preserved on the record under a key prefixed with an underscore.
rules: jurisdiction_level mapped into the six-value union; the delivered string kept as _jurisdiction_level_original.
domains: format-normalised, then any tag outside the 22 approved values prefixed "proposed:" as the spec directs. No semantic merging was done — that needs your call.

relationship_type: part_of edges moved onto the child node as part_of; contains edges reversed onto the child; produced_by edges dropped (publisher is a string, not a node); related_to / complements held in _dropped as deferred. Off-union values were poisoning every PageRank score with NaN.
last_updated added as null where absent (required field, string|null).
region filled with the country name where it was null or missing.
releases_per_year: unambiguous single-word cadences resolved to numbers; ambiguous text left in _cadence_original and listed under _gaps.unresolved_cadence.
source_kind mapped to official/commercial; delivered value kept as _source_kind_original.
Non-schema keys Grok wrote (shape, notes, referenced_by, ...) renamed with a leading underscore so they are visibly not part of the schema. Nothing deleted.

_gaps.note: What is genuinely missing and cannot be fixed mechanically — this is the research queue, not a defect list.
